name: Battle of Dien Bien Phu

phases.title: The French fortress and the Viet Minh ring
phases.text: The French held a central headquarters with strong points round it, and Isabelle to the south. The Viet Minh moved divisions and artillery into the hills round the valley and the French were completely surrounded.

phases.title: Béatrice is overrun
phases.text: The Viet Minh opened with a heavy bombardment of Béatrice, the northeastern outpost. The 312th Division then attacked, and by the early hours of 14 March the position had been taken.

phases.title: Gabrielle falls
phases.text: The 308th Division attacked Gabrielle from 20:00 on the night of 14 March after a heavy barrage. A French counterattack failed to relieve it, and the Algerian battalion fell back at 08:00 the next day.

phases.title: Anne-Marie is given up
phases.text: The fall of Béatrice and Gabrielle had demoralised the Tai troops. On the morning of 17 March, under cover of fog, most of them left or defected, and the French and the few Tais who remained withdrew from Anne-Marie.

phases.title: Dominique 1 and 2 are captured
phases.text: At 19:00 the 312th Division captured Dominique 1 and 2, outflanking all positions east of the river. French howitzers firing at zero elevation and anti-aircraft machine guns near the airfield then forced the attackers to retreat.

phases.title: Eliane 1 falls and Huguette 7 holds
phases.text: The 316th Division captured Eliane 1 and half of Eliane 2 by midnight. In the west the 308th Division attacked Huguette 7 and nearly broke through, but a French sergeant took charge of the defenders and sealed the breach.

phases.title: The French counterattack in the east
phases.text: The French retook Eliane 2 just after midnight. On the afternoon of 1 April a counterattack by everybody left who could be trusted to fight retook Dominique 2 and Eliane 1.

phases.title: The Viet Minh renew the assault
phases.text: The Viet Minh assaulted again and the exhausted French, who had no reserves, fell back from both positions late in the afternoon. A column sent north from Isabelle was attacked on the way and fell back to Isabelle.

phases.title: Eliane 2 holds and Huguette 7 is retaken
phases.text: The 316th Division attacked Eliane 2 and a few French tanks arrived from the central garrison and helped push it back. The Viet Minh briefly captured Huguette 7, then were pushed back by a French counterattack at dawn on 1 April.

phases.title: Sapping, and Eliane 1 retaken
phases.text: After heavy losses in the open on 5 April, Giáp turned to entrenchment and sapping. On 10 April the French retook Eliane 1 after it changed hands several times, and a Viet Minh attempt to regain it on 12 April was pushed back.

phases.title: Huguette 1 is overrun
phases.text: Viet Minh trenches almost surrounded Huguette 1 and 6. French sorties to supply Huguette 6 cost heavy casualties, the defenders of Huguette 6 broke out on 18 April, and Huguette 1 was overrun on 22 April.

phases.title: Eliane 1, Dominique 3 and Huguette 5 fall
phases.text: The Viet Minh attacked the exhausted defenders in mass on the night of 1 May and overran Eliane 1, Dominique 3 and Huguette 5. The French beat back the attacks on Eliane 2.

phases.title: Eliane 2 is mined and overrun
phases.text: The Viet Minh attacked Eliane 2 with Katyusha rockets and French artillery broke the first wave. Later that night a mine under Eliane 2 was detonated and within a few hours the defenders were overrun.

phases.title: The last attack on the headquarters
phases.text: Giáp ordered an all-out attack on the remaining French units. By evening enemy troops stood outside the headquarters bunker and the last radio report said the positions had been overrun.

note: The plan shows the whole siege, not a single day: the blocks are the strong points and the Viet Minh divisions. The positions of the strong points follow the compass directions the accounts give; the distances are not to scale except that Isabelle stands furthest south. The accounts do not say where each Viet Minh division stood before it attacked, so each is placed in the hills on the side of the strong point it is said to have attacked. Claudine, Eliane and the other numbered works are not drawn singly. Isabelle's end is told only as a breakout, so its block is left as it was. The relief column from Isabelle and the tanks are drawn as small parts of the garrison where they are named.
